reason: E1 and E2 directly support the link between LCO/lattice distortion, a rugged energy landscape, and elevated dislocation barriers/strength in the equiatomic alloy. However, no cited evidence addresses the effect of removing elements on LCO, lattice distortion, or mechanical properties in the quaternary/ternary subsets, leaving the core causal chain from element removal to reduced strength unsupported.
premises: Local chemical order (LCO) and lattice distortion create a rugged dislocation energy landscape in equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
This rugged landscape pins dislocations, raising the activation barrier for glide and increasing yield strength.
Removing elements reduces atomic-scale heterogeneity, thereby lowering LCO and lattice distortion.
Reduced heterogeneity lowers dislocation glide barriers and decreases yield strength relative to the equiatomic baseline.
The effect is systematic and moderate across quaternary and ternary alloys.
